clues: This small town is in Chad, in the Wadi Fira part of the land. It has its own court and is served by an airport.
This desert town has two clear times of year, dry and wet. Rain falls, then soon runs off in short-lived streams, while summer heat stays fierce and dry.
In the year 2004, a large wave of people fled the Darfur area and came to this town's lands. Most were of the same folk group as the town's own people.
Three big camps near this town hold more than sixty thousand folks who fled their homes. World aid groups work there to help and keep them safe.
The local folk are the Zaghawa, who live on both sides of the line with Sudan. They speak their own tongue and still look to their own Sultan as their chief.
